findings.title: LSASS memory accessed with full-read access masks by PowerShell and wsmprovhost
findings.summary: On scranton.dmevals.local, PowerShell.exe (PID 2976, user pbeesly) opened a handle to lsass.exe (PID 736) with GrantedAccess 0x1FFFFF (PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS) and 0x1F3FFF at 2020-05-02T03:05:16, i.e. full read/write of LSASS memory. The Security 4656 audit event for the same handle (AccessMask 0x1FFFFF) explicitly lists 'Read from process memory'. The same PowerShell session (user pbeesly) was executing credential/collection toolkit functions (Get-PrivateKeys, Get-Keystrokes, Invoke-ScreenCapture, Invoke-Persistence). Minutes later, on nashua.dmevals.local, wsmprovhost.exe (PID 7720, user pbeesly, spawned by Invoke-Command -ComputerName NASHUA) opened lsass.exe (PID 728) with GrantedAccess 0x1F3FFF at 2020-05-02T03:09:29. These are the classic access masks used to read LSASS memory for credential theft.

findings.title: No SAM/SECURITY hive dumping observed
findings.summary: No evidence of SAM/SECURITY registry hive theft. The only file-creation hits matching SAM/SECURITY were Prefetch files (SECURITYHEALTHSYSTRAY.EXE-*.pf etc.) created by svchost.exe, and the only registry writes to SAM/SECURITY were lsass.exe writing HKLM\SAM\SAM\Domains\Account\F and HKLM\SECURITY\Cache\NL$1 (normal lsass behaviour), plus LogonUI writing LoggedOnSAMUser. No reg save, no hive copies, no 4663/4656 handle requests to SAM objects by non-lsass processes.

findings.title: No NTDS.dit access observed
findings.summary: No hits for ntds.dit file creation/access, no diskshadow/vssadmin/esentutl command lines, and no NTDS-related service installs across sysmon, security, powershell and other datasets. No domain-controller credential theft activity was observed in this window.

findings.title: No LSA secrets dumping observed
findings.summary: No lsadump/secrets command lines, no SECURITY\Policy\Secrets registry access, and no credential-dumping service installs. The samlib.dll/cryptdll.dll image loads and the Lsa registry reads (AccessMask 0x1) are normal Windows component behaviour. The LSASS memory access by pbeesly's PowerShell is captured under T1003.001.

findings.title: No cached domain credential dumping observed
findings.summary: No cache/dcc2/mscache command lines or SECURITY\Cache handle requests by non-lsass processes. The HKLM\SECURITY\Cache\NL$1 writes are performed by lsass.exe itself (normal cached-credential maintenance), not by a dumping tool.

The genuinely suspicious activity observed (a hardcoded-credential exfil script by user pbeesly on scranton, and wsmprovhost.exe reading lsass with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff on nashua) is credential theft/exfiltration, which maps to other techniques (e.g. T1003/T1041), not MFA interception. findings.title: Broad LSASS access by wsmprovhost.exe on nashua - credential dumping, not MFA interception
findings.summary: On nashua.dmevals.local, wsmprovhost.exe (PID 7720, PowerShell remoting host) opened lsass.exe (PID 728) with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff, a broad mask including PROCESS_VM_READ, with a call trace through PowerShell management assemblies. This is consistent with credential dumping via PowerShell remoting (T1003), not MFA interception. It is reported as suspicious context; it does not demonstrate T1111.

Hunting for T1187 Forced Authentication across windows.security, windows.sysmon, windows.other and zeek produced no evidence of coercion of NTLM/Net-NTLMv2 authentication. The 121 event.code 5145 share-access events are all machine-account (NEWYORK$, SCRANTON$) reads of the \\*\SYSVOL share for GPO files (gpt.ini, Policies\{31B2F340-...}) — normal domain replication, not attacker-controlled shares. All 66 outbound SMB connections (destination.port 445) originate from the System process to the DC 10.0.0.4 / link-local fe80::e40c:95b6:b0a7:6429, i.e. normal domain traffic. The only .lnk files created are benign: two Explorer 'Recent' shortcuts on scranton (Backup and Restore (Windows 7).lnk, System and Security.lnk) and a StartUp shortcut hostui.lnk dropped by PowerShell as part of a separate fileless-payload chain (hostui.exe -> powershell Get-ItemPropertyValue HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Javasoft | Invoke-Expression), which is execution/persistence, not forced authentication. The only UNC path usage is PsExec64.exe \\NASHUA with explicit credentials (-u dmevals\pbeesly -p ...), i.e. credential-based lateral movement, not auth coercion. No .scf/.url/.searchConnector-ms/.library-ms lures and no WebDAV (@SSL/DavWWWRoot) references were found. The single windows.other NTLM event (6038) is an informational per-boot notice that NTLM is in use, not a coercion attempt.
findings.title: No forced-authentication (T1187) activity observed; SMB/UNC traffic is normal domain and credential-based lateral movement
